entities.summary:
Alexandre-Théodore-Victor, comte de Lameth (1760-10-28, Paris - 1829-03-18) was a French soldier and politician who played a pivotal role in the Siege of Toulon, where he successfully defended the city against the British, earning him recognition and appointment as a member of the French Directory.

 As a key figure in the early modern period, de Lameth was part of the French Revolutionary Wars and supported the Jacobin faction, advocating for the execution of King Louis XVI.

 His military experience and leadership skills led to his involvement in the French Directory, which aimed to stabilize the new government after the revolution.


 Alexandre-Théodore-Victor, comte de Lameth was a French soldier and politician who served as a commander in the French Revolutionary Wars. Born in Paris in 1760, he played a key role in the Siege of Toulon, where he successfully defended the city against the British. His military experience and leadership skills earned him recognition, and he was appointed as a member of the French Directory. As a politician, he supported the Jacobin faction and was a vocal advocate for the execution of King Louis XVI.

 His legacy extends to the modern era, influencing the development of French politics and the country's role in European affairs.

 In the context of the French Revolution, de Lameth's actions reflect the tumultuous period of political upheaval and social change that shaped modern France.
